'''Sabacc game mode Dune Sea decks''' are draft sample decks for the Dune Sea table of the [[Sabacc game mode outline]]: one Light Side and one Dark Side deck, a ladder of Jawa dealers with their decks, a boss deck for each side, and what an unequal dealer deck does to the house edge.

''Status: planning and draft. Every card below is a real Decipher card; the decks are examples, not final lists.''

== How the decks are built ==

* '''Target.''' Each deck has the same 60-card spread as the standard fair deck, [[Sabacc game mode outline#Standard deck (decided)|Deck C]]: 19 / 10 / 3 / 1 / 5 / 11 / 5 / 6 cards of value 0 to 7.
* '''Values.''' A card's value is the destiny number printed on it. Location cards have a destiny of zero.<ref name="ar2023">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook] (2023): destiny draws (PDF page 30) and Appendix C, Sabacc.</ref> The pages of virtual cards often show no destiny number, so only Decipher cards are used.
* '''Premise cards.''' Bill's starting premise is Jawas, sandcrawlers, Jawa weapons, and droids. Cards for these, and the locations named for Jawas, the Dune Sea, or sandcrawlers, are listed as ''premise cards''. Other Tatooine locations and Tatooine- or Dune Sea-flavoured creatures, vehicles, devices, and characters fill the gaps and are listed separately.
* '''Copies.''' The rulebook gives no copy limit that applies here. The drafts assume at most 3 copies of a card, and 2 of a unique (•) card.
* '''No sabacc Interrupt.''' [[Dune Sea Sabacc]] itself (value 5) is left out, as it starts the game.

== Cards available ==

Tatooine locations are the 0s: 26 Light Side and 22 Dark Side titles, counting the Tatooine systems and the sandcrawler sites. Premise cards other than locations are few and sit at 1 to 6. The only premise card worth 7 is the Dark Side [[Double Laser Cannon]], a sandcrawler weapon; the Light Side has none, and the other 7s that fit the theme are weak.

== Wild and clone cards ==

In [[Dune Sea Sabacc]] the wild cards (0–7) are sandcrawler sites, [[Magnetic Suction Tube]], [[Jawa Siesta]], and [[Jawa Pack]]. The clone cards are Tatooine locations, sandcrawlers, Jawa weapons, and [[Utinni!]].<ref name="dsabacc">[[Dune Sea Sabacc]] and [[Dune Sea Sabacc (Dark)]] game text.</ref> The Light Side draft above has 1 wild card and 21 clone cards; the Dark Side draft has 1 wild card and 23 clone cards. With the option button off, every card counts as its printed value and the odds below apply. With it on, more than a third of each deck becomes clone or wild, which changes the odds. That setting is not modelled.

== Too many Jawas ==

The Jawa cards are worth 2 or 3, and Deck C has only three 2s and one 3. A deck that follows Deck C exactly can hold about four Jawas. A deck with many Jawas needs a different spread. One draft, a Jawa-heavy spread of 14 / 6 / 5 / 12 / 6 / 8 / 5 / 4 (about half the deck is premise cards: 31 Light, 32 Dark), moves the odds a lot:

{| class="wikitable"
! Player deck !! Dealer deck !! House edge !! Player win / push / loss %
|-
| Deck C || Deck C || −1.79% || 49.4 / 3.0 / 47.6
|-
| Jawa-heavy || Jawa-heavy || −3.07% || 49.7 / 3.7 / 46.6
|-
| Jawa-heavy || Deck C || −9.39% || 53.5 / 3.6 / 42.9
|-
| Deck C || Jawa-heavy || 8.43% || 43.4 / 3.7 / 53.0
|}

A player with Jawas and a dealer without them is far ahead; the reverse favours the house heavily. [[Jawa Ion Gun]] is worth 3, so it appears only in the Jawa-heavy drafts, whose lists are at the end of this page.

== Dealer's deck and the house edge ==

With the card game's rules (see [[Sabacc game mode outline#Going over 11 and ties (decided)|Going over 11 and ties]]) and the same deck on both sides, the committed dealer (draws on 7 or less) leaves the player ahead by 1.8%. Giving the dealer a different deck, shown openly, can restore a house edge of 2 to 2.5%. The player keeps Deck C.

{| class="wikitable"
! Dealer's deck !! Cards of value 0 to 7 !! Total !! House edge !! Player win / push / loss %
|-
| Deck C (no change) || 19, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 60 || −1.79% || 49.4 / 3.0 / 47.6
|-
| Add 2 zeros || 21, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 62 || −3.14% || 50.0 / 2.8 / 47.2
|-
| Add 4 zeros || 23, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 64 || −4.49% || 50.6 / 2.7 / 46.7
|-
| Remove 6 zeros || 13, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 54 || 2.17% || 47.8 / 3.3 / 48.9
|-
| Swap 2 zeros for 2 fives || 17, 10, 3, 1, 5, 13, 5, 6 || 60 || 1.93% || 47.7 / 3.2 / 49.1
|-
| Swap 2 zeros for 2 threes || 17, 10, 3, 3, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 60 || 1.08% || 47.8 / 3.2 / 48.9
|-
| '''Swap 3 zeros for 3 threes (Jawas)''' || 16, 10, 3, 4, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 60 || 2.34% || 47.2 / 3.3 / 49.5
|-
| Swap 3 ones for 3 threes || 19, 7, 3, 4, 5, 11, 5, 6 || 60 || 2.04% || 47.4 / 3.2 / 49.4
|-
| Swap 5 sevens for 5 zeros || 24, 10, 3, 1, 5, 11, 5, 1 || 60 || 2.31% || 46.9 / 2.6 / 50.5
|}

Method: exact calculation with endless decks, the dealer drawing on 7 or less and never looking at the player's hand, the player using the best hit or stand at every step, perfect sabacc paying double both ways, six cards at most, wild and clone cards not modelled. An endless-deck simulation of 1,000,000 hands of the same strategy for the Deck C row and the bold row agrees with the exact figures within its margin of error (about 0.1 points). One finite 60-card deck was not simulated for these decks. A negative edge means the player is ahead. Details are on the [[Talk:Sabacc game mode outline|talk page]].

Adding zeros to the dealer's deck does the opposite of what one might expect: the player gains. A likely reason is that the dealer draws more cards before he stands. The edge comes from giving the dealer fewer zeros or more mid-sized cards. The bold row replaces three locations with three Jawas worth 3, which fits the theme and brings the house to about 2.3%. If equal card counts went to the dealer instead of a draw, the same deck would give the house about 5.4%, so that tie rule would need a weaker dealer deck.

== Boss decks ==

'''R'kik D'nec (Light Side boss).''' [[R'kik D'nec, Hero Of The Dune Sea]] is a Jawa whose card says: "When he is playing Dune Sea Sabacc and wins, he wins double." His deck list is under [[#Boss deck lists|Boss deck lists]]; it has the 16 / 10 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 11 / 5 / 6 spread, a house edge of 2.34% before his card text. The text is a large number if read literally:

{| class="wikitable"
! How R'kik's double works !! House edge
|-
| No double (deck only) || 2.34%
|-
| 1 win in 20 doubles || 4.59%
|-
| 1 win in 10 doubles || 6.84%
|-
| 1 win in 4 doubles || 13.59%
|-
| Every win doubles (card text read literally) || 47.32%
|-
| Doubles only when he finishes on exactly 11 || 12.18%
|}

Each 1% of his wins that double adds about 0.45 points of house edge. A boss that doubles every win is practically unbeatable, so the double would have to be a rare, visible event or tied to the stake.

'''Iasa (Dark Side boss).''' [[Iasa, The Traitor Of Jawa Canyon]] has a Dune Sea Sabacc text close to Lando's: "When playing Dune Sea Sabacc, may subtract 1 from or add 1 to your total." His deck list is under [[#Boss deck lists|Boss deck lists]]. The table gives the house edge against Deck C if he may adjust on a share of hands. He moves his finished total one step toward 11, which is never worse for him, so the numbers are the same whether or not he sees the player's hand, as for Lando:

{| class="wikitable"
! Share of hands where he adjusts !! Deck C for both sides !! Dealer deck with three more Jawas
|-
| 0% || −1.79% || 2.34%
|-
| 5% || 0.27% || 4.36%
|-
| 10% || 2.33% || 6.38%
|-
| 25% || 8.51% || 12.42%
|-
| 50% || 18.78% || 22.47%
|-
| 100% || 39.19% || 42.46%
|}

== Contenders and decks (draft) ==

''Status: planning and draft, for Bill to review. The order of the ladder is a proposal and may be changed.''

Every Dune Sea dealer below is a unique Jawa character. The decks follow Bill's rules: real Decipher cards, at most 3 copies of a card (2 of a unique card), the dealer's own card in the deck, and the cards of one contender's deck kept out of the other contenders' decks where the pool allows. The boss decks may use the earlier contenders' cards.

All the decks here use the dealer spread 16 / 10 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 11 / 5 / 6 (the three extra 3s replace three 0s of [[#Dealer's deck and the house edge|the dealer's deck above]]). Against a player on Deck C, with the card-game rules, a dealer who draws on 7 or less, and a perfect sabacc paying 2:1, the house edge is 2.34% (exact, endless deck). A simulation of two separate 60-card decks, each reshuffled every hand, over 4,000,000 hands gave 2.39% ± 0.06. Every deck has the same spread, so every deck has the same base edge. The cards differ, and the bosses add a perk. Wild and clone cards are not modelled.

=== Boss deck lists ===

The two boss decks use the same spread, so each starts at the same 2.34% before the boss's perk.

'''Light Side boss: R'kik D'nec'''
R'kik is worth 1 and has 2 copies. His own 3s slot holds four of the five earlier contenders ([[Het Nkik]], [[Uutkik]], [[Thedit]], and [[Aved Luun]]) and the 2s hold [[Kalit]] ×2 and [[Kalit's Sandcrawler]], so all five earlier Jawas appear. The 0s add [[Tatooine: Dune Sea]], the site of his lore, and the 5s and 6s use the strongest premise cards. The four 3s leave no room for [[Jawa Ion Gun]], which his text would deploy free; that would need one contender swapped out. The Virtual Set 8 version, [[R'kik D'nec, Hero Of The Dune Sea (V) (Virtual Set 8)]], has no Sabacc text, so the deck uses the Jabba's Palace card.

'''Dark Side boss: Iasa'''
Iasa is worth 1 and has 2 copies. The 2s hold [[Wittin]], [[Dathcha]], and [[Wittin's Sandcrawler]], and the 3s hold [[Daroe]], [[Nebit]], [[Herat]], and one [[Jawa (Dark)|Jawa]], so all five earlier Jawas appear. His own text takes 3 from the target's defense value when he fires a Jawa weapon, so [[Jawa Blaster]] ×2 is included, and [[Tatooine: Jawa Canyon (Dark)|Jawa Canyon]] is in the 0s because of his title. The 6s and 7s are as thin as in the Level 1 deck.

30 premise cards, 27 other Tatooine-flavoured cards, and 3 weak fits (†); 46 different cards. With the option button on, 1 cards are wild and 20 are clone cards. Weak fits: †[[Aurra Sing's Blaster Rifle]] and †[[Hunting Party]] at 7.


'''Boss perks.''' Iasa's adjustment is modelled as the dealer moving his finished total one step toward 11 on a share of hands. Moving toward 11 is never worse for him, so the figure is the same whether or not he sees the player's hand. R'kik's double is modelled as a share of his wins that pay double. Proposal for a cap: one hand in ten for either boss, about 6.4% for Iasa and 6.8% for R'kik, against 2.34% for the contenders. One hand in twenty gives about 4.4% and 4.6%. The tables under [[#Boss decks|Boss decks]] have the full range.

The 0s, 1s, 5s, and 7s run short; the 2s, 3s, 4s, and 6s do not. The 7s are the worst: each side has only 3 titles with a Tatooine link that are worth 7, allowing 7 copies in all (the fourth title in each column is an artillery card with no Tatooine link). Only the 3s, with the Jawa characters, have room for real variety. Every contender can still have its own cards at 2, 3, 4, and 6, and the 0s differ by the location sets.

How the number of decks changes this (borrowed cards over all contender decks):

|-
| 4 || 53 || 60
|-
| 5 || 97 || 108

With 3 contender decks plus the boss, nothing but the 7s and a few 1s repeat. With 5, each of the later decks repeats roughly 20 to 30 cards, mostly 0s, 1s, 5s, and 7s. That is the trade-off for keeping all five Jawas.

== Open questions ==

* The copy limit for sabacc decks (3 and 2 are assumptions).
* Whether the 7s may use weak-fit cards, or the Dune Sea spread should shift to values the theme can fill.
* Which house-edge tool to use: a dealer deck with three extra Jawas (about 2.3%), a boss perk, or both.
* How wild and clone cards change the odds when the option button is on.
* Whether the sabacc Interrupt itself belongs in a themed deck.
* The ladder order, and whether the Light Side and Dark Side ladders should mirror each other.
* Whether to keep all five contenders per side (about 20 to 30 repeated cards in each later deck) or cut to three or four, which keeps nearly every card exclusive.
* Whether the 1s and 7s may use weak-fit cards, since the pool has almost no Jawa cards worth 1 and very few worth 7.
* The boss perks: how often R'kik's double and Iasa's adjustment may happen (proposal: one hand in ten).
* Whether to add a sixth, non-Jawa dealer per side.
